concept_html:
Spark splits DataFrame operations into two kinds.

  • Transformations build a plan and return a new DataFrame at once: filter, select, withColumn, join, groupBy().agg(). Nothing is read yet.
  • Actions run the plan and return a result: count(), collect(), show(), first(), toPandas(), and every write.

This is lazy evaluation. It lets the optimiser see the whole plan before running it, so it can push filters into the file scan and skip columns you never use.

The cost is easy to miss: each action runs the whole plan again, from the source. Nothing is kept between actions unless you ask for it. A local test shows it plainly: a Python function counted its own calls inside a plan over 1,000 rows. After the first count(), it had run 1,000 times. After a second count(), 2,000.

Your reference data-contract validator calls count() more than ten times on the same uncached DataFrame: once for the row count, once per mandatory column, once per key and so on. Each call rereads the delivery from storage.

Three fixes, in order of preference:

  1. Combine the questions into one action. One agg with many expressions answers them all in a single pass:

python df.agg( F.count("*").alias("rows"), F.count_if(F.col("final_weight").isNull()).alias("null_weights"), F.sum("final_weight").alias("weight_sum"), ).collect()[0]

  1. Materialise an expensive intermediate result to a Delta table, then read that table for the follow-up actions.
  2. Cache with df.cache() on classic clusters only. Serverless compute, which Free Edition uses, does not support cache APIs.

lines: def check_delivery(df: DataFrame) -> dict[str, int]:
"""Row, null and distinct counts for a delivery in one pass."""
row = df.agg(
F.count("*").alias("rows"),
F.count_if(F.col("respondent_id").isNull()).alias("null_ids"),
F.count_if(F.col("final_weight").isNull()).alias("null_weights"),
F.count_distinct("respondent_id").alias("distinct_ids"),
).collect()[0]

solution_lines: def table_health(df: DataFrame) -> dict[str, float | int | None]:
"""Row count, null counts and weight range in one pass over df."""
row = df.agg(
F.count("*").alias("rows"),
F.count_if(F.col("respondent_id").isNull()).alias("null_ids"),
F.count_if(F.col("final_weight").isNull()).alias("null_weights"),
F.min("final_weight").alias("min_weight"),
F.max("final_weight").alias("max_weight"),
).collect()[0]

title: Lazy evaluation, and why every count() re-runs the plan
why_html:
A contract validator checks a 40-million-row delivery with 23 separate count() calls, one per check. Each call rescans the source files in cloud storage. The validation step takes 38 minutes, longer than the transform it protects, and the team starts skipping it "for small redeliveries". A redelivery with duplicated keys then goes straight to silver.

Rewritten as one agg with 23 expressions, the same checks run in a single scan of about two minutes, and nobody has a reason to skip them.
